To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the scope and the role of requirements engineering in agile system development depend on the system development context and b) the key challenges in large-scale agile development are to manage knowledge about customer value and to align the requirements model with agile methods.

requirements engineering and agile practices can be successfully combined in large-scale system developments if the requirements are modeled holistically and if the requirements model is aligned with agile practices.

a) agile development in large-scale system projects can only succeed if requirements engineering and agile software development practices are aligned, and b) a holistic requirements model that covers all relevant aspects and their interplay can help achieve this alignment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to integrate requirements engineering and agile development in large-scale systems development.
the question: What are the challenges of requirements engineering in large-scale agile system development?
how agile methods can be successfully applied to software-intense large-scale systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the agile manifesto is not applicable in large-scale systems engineering, but rather the opposite, i.e., the principles of agile methods can be applied to large-scale systems engineering.
requirements engineering is still needed in large-scale agile system development.
agile methods are not a panacea but a valuable tool to increase the quality and efficiency of software-intensive system development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
requirements engineering in the agile context needs to be redefined as a continuous process of learning about the system, its environment, and the customer needs.
the requirements engineer is not only a facilitator for the development of the software, but a mediator between customer value and the development of software.
the requirements engineering community should not be afraid of agile development but rather should be more active in supporting agile development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the agile manifesto is a good starting point, but it is not enough.
requirements engineering needs to be more closely coupled with the software development process to enable continuous integration and continuous deployment of software-intensive, large-scale systems.
the requirements discipline needs to adapt its practices in large-scale agile system development.
